4.3.1.5.3 Concepts of data access
Tables 4.9 and 4.10 summarize the characteristics of implicit versus explicit data reception and transmission. Implicit Read Explicit Read Receiving of data element values is performed only once when runnable starts Runnable decides when and how often a data element value is received Values of data elements do not change while runnable is running. Runnable can always decide to receive the latest value Several API calls to the same signal always yield the same data element value Several API calls to the same signal may yield different data element values Runnable must terminate (all categories) Runnable is of cat. 1B or 2 Table 4.9: Implicit vs. explicit read Implicit Write Explicit Write Sending of data element values is only done once after runnable returns Runnable can decide when sending of data element values is done via the API call Several usages of the API call inside the runnable cause only one data element transmission Several usages of the API call inside the runnable cause several transmissions of the data element content. (Depending on the behavior of COM, the number of API calls and the number of transmissions are not necessarily equal.) Runnable must terminate (all categories) Runnable is cat. 1B or 2 Table 4.10: Implicit vs. explicit write
